title: David wasn’t fearless.
paragraphs:
Goliath saw a boy with no armor.
David saw a God with no equal.
“I come to you in the name of the LORD of hosts…” (1 Samuel 17:45)

Fear says, Look how big the giant is.
Faith says, Look who stands with me.

David’s courage was not borrowed from self-confidence.
It was born from God-confidence.
And some of us keep waiting to feel brave before we obey.

Victory in Scripture never begins with human strength.
It begins with holy focus.
Eyes locked on God.
Heart anchored in His name.
Soul convinced that the battle is bigger than flesh and blood.

David did not run at Goliath because he felt nothing.
He ran because he believed something.

You may be facing a giant today—sin, fear, shame, addiction, rejection, the voice that tells you you’ll never rise again.
Do not worship the size of what stands against you.
Fix your eyes on the God who fights for His glory.

And even deeper—
David points us to Jesus.

Because one greater than David stepped onto the battlefield for us.
Not with a sling.
With a cross.

Jesus faced the giant we could never defeat—sin, death, hell itself.
And by His sacrifice and resurrection, He won the victory in our place.
So now we do not fight for acceptance.
We fight from victory already secured by Christ.

Fear may still whisper.
But faith answers with a name.
